transition.reacquire_runtime.name: Acquire exact locked unified Techne.Loom.Runtime.<rid> package (Skill Orchestrator)
transition.reacquire_runtime.description: Pause for host acquisition, integrity validation, and safe extraction of the exact locked unified Techne.Loom.Runtime.<rid> package for the detected RID, used by the Skill Orchestrator module through `loom skill`. Follow the L0-L6 order in reference/execution-contract.md. A direct in-process .NET `HttpClient` call from PowerShell is L3; PowerShell `Invoke-WebRequest`/`Invoke-RestMethod`, curl, gh, wget, BITS, and other shell/network download CLIs are L6; nuget.exe is the sole earlier CLI exception. After any failed request, do not automatically switch transports to repeat the same artifact/source. A nonblocked source may be retried only as an explicit L6 operation after L0-L5 are exhausted and the user approves that exact CLI action. If the source or request is explicitly blocked or denied by network/security policy, stop all attempts to that source through every transport; continue only with an independently configured and approved fallback source, otherwise stop and report the blocker. If the user denies CLI approval, stop and do not switch tools or sources to evade that decision. Never install runtimes or downloaders. Under the Exact NuGet Acquisition Completion Rule, a missing exact package is downloaded by a run-scoped program on an already-installed runtime's in-process HTTP API, retries re-run that program, an approved L6 CLI is allowed only when no such runtime exists, and every stop or blocker outcome above keeps this step paused and resumable until the same exact version is downloaded and verified; it never ends the run or records a terminal failure. Return exact package/apphost evidence before the first runtime call, and set runtime_preflight_result to ready only after package identity/version/RID, SHA-512, manifest/archive, safe extraction, and apphost checks pass; failures cannot reach guide capture.

parameters.skillHint:
Run the local workflow designer at assets/agents/loom-skill-enhancement-workflow-designer.agent.md. Consume the bounded referencePackManifest, schemaDemoInput, and phaseDesignPolicy before authoring. Count authored states only; at 40 or more, freeze and check a typed skeleton, then author isolated phases capped at 25 states as a soft limit. Use the same selected unified `loom` apphost through the `loom skill` route for `skeleton-check`, `phase-compile`, `impact`, `merge`, and `loom skill compile`. Phase compilation is static only. Aggregate interface changes, revalidate affected phases, merge into a new candidate, and fully compile that exact candidate; never migrate a live workflow. Cap repairs at three attempts per phase and two after-merge compile rounds. Return phase_design_evidence linked to phaseDesignEvidence inside the existing static-contract-review.json; do not create a fourth report. Return the checked-in template, dispatch record, gate review, and the three runtime-owned workflow-design records. Save those records outside the skill bundle and use verified relative evidence references. Consume evidenceNodeMapAnalysis and map the skill being enhanced's SKILL.md first as Priority 1. For each new or changed context_fields entry, compare its JSON/container type with an independent actual SO producer output or authoritative producer schema. Run `loom skill inspect-contract-fragment --contract-file <owning-contract> --json-pointer /context_fields` and a minimal same-apphost probe before broad tests; the catalog echo alone does not prove business types. Record contextFieldTypeComparisons in static-contract-review.json; unknown type evidence blocks readiness. Development-support reference, schema/demo, candidate, plan, and context hashes are optional generated metadata; do not calculate, compare, re-attest, freshness-check, or gate on them while consuming. Exact package SHA-512 and target-business artifact hashes explicitly required by the contract remain mandatory. Also require the skill being enhanced's own SKILL.md and any applicable local workflow-authoring agent prompts or template hints to use this same apphost-owned Build(WorkflowScriptInput) and Edit(WorkflowInstance, WorkflowScriptInput) route for its own workflow and future revisions: keep complete workflow JSON in external files, let the selected unified `loom` apphost use its `loom skill` route to read and deserialize it and write the canonical workflow JSON, and keep file I/O and JSON parsing out of scripts. Do not add this workflow-maintenance rule to unrelated domain-business prompts.

[enhancement-continuation-v1]
By default, continue a bounded enhancement request through routine planning, edits, repair, validation, and completion without asking for facts already available from the source pack or ordinary reversible choices. Ask only for a necessary user-owned value or decision that cannot be inferred, genuine human approval explicitly required by the route, or a policy or security stop. Never present agent-generated content as human approval. For synthetic-scenario validation, record each scenario's isolated inputs, expected result, pass condition, observed evidence, and separate verdict; label synthetic evidence and never claim it is human approval or a live external result. Parallelize only independent isolated cases after checking shared resource limits; serialize or batch dependent or shared-state cases. Aggregate only after all expected results arrive, coordinate one repair pass, then rerun only checks affected by changes. Do not add scenario templates or nodes unless the graph contract requires them.

parameters.skillHint:
Present the compiled audit artifacts and collect approval_decision plus feedback_notes. Use the user's requested language. When the host identifies autopilot or unattended mode, do not call a blocking user-input tool, open a browser, or wait. Only for a session that does not require genuine human approval, if the same active AskUser session has an endpoint returned by the runtime (`ask_user` payload `endpoints` for SO), use only that endpoint and the supported HTTP session/submission flow: read the active contract, infer type-valid answers from available workflow context, and submit them. Do not start a second worker, guess a URL, or expose pairing/session credentials. Clearly warn that the answers were agent-generated while the user was unavailable and are not user-confirmed. Never infer or claim genuine human approval, and never submit an agent-generated approval decision as human consent. A validated runtime receipt proves submission, not genuine human approval. If this AskUser requires genuine human approval, do not submit an agent-generated approval via HTTP or result-file continuation and do not consume the active session; provide clearly warned suggestions only and leave the workflow and any session waiting for the human's actual approval. Preserve the user-absence explanation in a caller-provided additional-context field when writable, or in question context before the session starts; never try to modify an active ask contract, invent ask wire fields, or disguise the note as an answer. Warn in the result if no writable field exists. If no usable endpoint or HTTP submission is possible, skip the interactive ask, generate the best-supported answers and warn, but never fabricate a receipt or bypass owning-runtime validation. For structured AskUser, continue only when the owning runtime accepts a real validated receipt. For unstructured AskUser that does not require genuine human approval, use only a supported noninteractive continuation that passes owning-runtime validation. If the required receipt or supported continuation is unavailable, explain that the workflow remains waiting. Outside autopilot, for unstructured AskUser, use the normal host-approved interactive user-input handoff. Do not expect an AskUser worker endpoint or receipt; resume with the user's answer using a supported result-file continuation that passes owning-runtime validation. For structured AskUser, read the endpoint from the same SO runtime-returned structured result (`ask_user` payload `endpoints` for SO) and use only endpoint URLs returned by the runtime. Use loopback only when the embedded browser can reach the worker host; otherwise use only a host-provided, approved HTTPS reverse-proxy candidate. Select routes using the embedded browser network context, not shell or worker reachability. Never rewrite a hostname, infer a public address from untrusted forwarded headers, or create a tunnel. Open the selected URL itself only through the initiating agent embedded-browser capability; never instruct the CLI, runtime, worker, or OS URL handler to launch a desktop browser. Treat the full endpoint URL, including any one-time pairing fragment, as a secret; pass it directly to the embedded browser and keep it out of logs, progress text, audit artifacts, and ordinary output. If no returned approved route is reachable, leave the ask pending. If embedded browsing is unavailable but an approved route is reachable, provide an explicit user-action handoff using that route.

[human-approval-boundary-v1]
Do not ask for facts available from the source pack or ordinary reversible choices. Preserve this step only for the declared user-owned feedback and genuine human approval decision; never infer or synthesize approval. If approval is required but unavailable, keep the workflow waiting.

parameters.content:
# Governance Verdict
- Verdict rule: this manifest summarizes governed completion only when the mapped runtime-owned evidence families below already exist on the official runnable route; it does not create replacement route-proof evidence inside this terminal step.
- Current status: completed on the terminal official runnable route that emitted this manifest.
- Current node: state.done
- Final Done reached: yes on the route that emitted this manifest.
- Missing evidence rule: any null or missing mapped evidence family below must be reported as missing evidence and blocks a compliant interpretation outside this manifest.
- Next action: use commit_report_ready and this runtime-owned completion manifest for final handoff.

# Evidence Checklist
- workflow_runtime_copy_json: runtime-owned workflow copy for the official run chain.
- event_log_file: runtime-owned event log for the same chain.
- review_fix_loop_evidence: prerequisite review and fix lineage for this slice.
- commit_report_ready: completion-time handoff readiness evidence.
- checked_in_skill_markdown_asset: SKILL.md remains the authoritative checked-in source deliverable.
- checked_in_package_lock_asset: assets/so-workflow/so-package-lock.json remains the authoritative checked-in runtime lock.
- node_to_file_map: assets/so-workflow/node-to-file-map.md remains the authoritative node-to-artifact map.
- internal_document_evidence: target-local document snapshots and manifest provenance were inspected under the declared root of the skill being enhanced.
- requested_checked_in_deliverables: SKILL.md, reference/execution-contract.md, reference/so-skill-reference.md, reference/review-and-evidence-contract.md, assets/so-workflow/contract.json, assets/so-workflow/so-package-lock.json, assets/so-workflow/so-template.json, assets/so-workflow/governance-notes.md, assets/so-workflow/node-to-file-map.md, and `assets/agents/workflow-designer-01-authority.md`, `assets/agents/workflow-designer-02-runtime.md`, and `assets/agents/workflow-designer-05-validation.md`. Their checked-in paths are listed in node_to_file_map; this manifest points to the existing internal_document_evidence and node_to_file_map records and does not copy or recreate them.
- completion_manifest_reference: this runtime-owned manifest reference anchors the final verdict surface.
- completion_manifest_md: this human-reviewable manifest is the fixed governance verdict and evidence checklist surface.
- workflow_dataflow_json: runtime-owned dataflow report for the same official run or resume.
- skill_plan_md: runtime-owned per-run plan at <execution-output-root>/plan/skill-plan.md.
- governance_notes_md: checked-in governance-notes.md source reference in node_to_file_map.
- mermaid_delivery: verified Mermaid, HTML, Analysis, and Dataflow delivery evidence.
- batch_repair_evidence: the single coordinated pre-validation repair record.
- aggregated_post_fix_validation: the complete aggregate of every post-fix validator result.
- serial_validation_evidence: the final ordered serial validation result.

This manifest summarizes governed completion from the existing runtime-owned evidence families. It does not replace those evidence families, it does not claim to recreate checked-in source deliverables, and it does not self-certify route-proof evidence that was absent before the terminal step.

failureGuidance.summary: Exact package acquisition is blocked or lacks complete package identity, integrity, archive, extraction, or apphost evidence.
failureGuidance.nextAction: Start with L0 local artifacts and caches: reuse the fully validated shared SO cache, then the standard NuGet cache. On a complete miss, follow the ordered L0-L6 policy in reference/execution-contract.md and its Exact NuGet Acquisition Completion Rule: a missing exact package is downloaded, never a reason to end; when L0-L2 miss, write and run a run-scoped download program on an already-installed runtime's in-process HTTP API outside source and skill folders instead of calling a shell/CLI downloader directly. For exact NuGet packages, that rule overrides the generic retry and stop wording below: retries re-run the same runtime program, an approved L6 CLI is allowed only when no installed runtime offers an in-process HTTP API, and every stop or blocker outcome keeps this step in a resumable acquisition-pending pause that asks the user for an approved way forward and then resumes acquiring the same exact version; it never ends the run, marks it complete, or records a terminal failure. After any failed request, do not automatically switch transports to repeat the same artifact/source. A nonblocked source may be retried only as an explicit L6 operation after L0-L5 are exhausted and the user approves that exact CLI action. If the source or request is explicitly blocked or denied by network/security policy, stop all attempts to that source through every transport; continue only with an independently configured and approved fallback source, otherwise stop and report the blocker. If the user denies CLI approval, stop and do not switch tools or sources to evade that decision. L6 includes PowerShell `Invoke-WebRequest`/`Invoke-RestMethod`, `curl`, `gh`, `wget`, BITS, and other shell/network CLIs; a direct in-process .NET `HttpClient` call from PowerShell is L3; `nuget.exe` is the sole earlier CLI exception. Never install a runtime or downloader. OS/network security controls remain authoritative. Preserve failed evidence, and set runtime_preflight_result to ready only after the locked package ID/version/detected RID and source-specific integrity checks pass: NuGet-origin .nupkg bytes match only `packageHash` from the exact version registration `catalogEntry`, with no separate NuGet .nupkg.sha512 sidecar; GitHub fallback follows the exact-version .nupkg.sha512 link in the selected package index, verifies the link resolves, and compares its checksum only with the downloaded GitHub package bytes. Do not require cross-source hash equality. Archive safety, safe extraction, and apphost checks must also pass; any denial, block, failure, or incomplete result must not reach guide capture.

A direct in-process .NET `HttpClient` call from PowerShell is L3; its web cmdlets are L6. Approval must name the exact tool, source/host, artifact and version, destination, and purpose; it is not reusable for another operation. If approved PowerShell 5.1 web cmdlets are used, add `-UseBasicParsing`; this does not change the L6 approval requirement.

evidenceReferences.quote: Use an explicit `TransitionGroup` with `strategy: whenAllPass` for independent external `SubagentCall` reviews and validations that share one join state. The SO runtime registers every expected transition in one persisted batch and keeps the workflow at the current state until every result has been returned. A missing or duplicate result fails closed. Use this only for independent external transitions; keep synchronous mutations and ordered checks in separate serial groups. Legacy wire value `all` must be migrated and must not be authored.
